exposure: Febrile urinary tract infection (UTI) status (present or absent)
outcome: Gut microbiota composition (beta diversity, alpha diversity, relative abundance of genera)
cohort: The study included 42 febrile neonates younger than 2 months, comprising 17 with and 25 without febrile urinary tract infection, admitted to the pediatric ward.
finding: Febrile neonates with urinary tract infection (UTI) exhibited a significantly different fecal microbiota beta-diversity and distinct differences in relative abundance of the 20 most prevalent genera compared to febrile neonates without UTI, though alpha diversity did not differ.
cross-section timing: At admission to the pediatric ward for febrile illness.
